title: W3 unresolved: growth_district_live_count's Terminal-only filter is still unpinned — a routers-count-too mutation passes all 261 tests
detail: P2 gap, carried from r1 W3 and not touched by the fold. The cap's denominator semantics (routers never consume district budget) rest on an unpinned predicate; the suite cannot detect a regression.

title: Fractional-anchor pin exercises fractional inputs but does not discriminate the scale-10 quantization — MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE=1 passes it
evidence: map_test.odin:624-627: `append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = "A", kind = .City, pos = {6.4, 6.3}})` / `append(&b.districts, Map_District{name = "B", kind = .Suburb, pos = {24.6, 6.1}})` with asserts only for (15,6)→A and (20,6)→B. Mutation run: `MAP_ANCHOR_SCALE :: 10` → `:: 1` → `Finished 261 tests in 5.288751s. All tests were successful.` (both tiles keep the same assignment under raw integral anchors: 81 vs 81 tie→A; 196 vs 16→B).
detail: r1 N8's core concern — the quantization path never distinguishes — persists in subtler form: fractional anchors now parse, but the chosen tiles cannot detect a scale regression at unit level.
recommended_fix: Add one tile whose nearest anchor flips between scale-10 quantized and integral anchors (e.g. anchors at x.4/x.6 straddling a midpoint) and assert the quantized winner.
